name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
description: A white field between narrow red bands at top and bottom, charged at the centre with the crowned quartered royal arms: the Polish White Eagle alternating with the Lithuanian Vytis.
history: Banner of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth (1569–1795), one of early-modern Europe's largest states, quartering the emblems of its two constituent nations under the royal crown.

features.role: crowned arms quartering the White Eagle and the Vytis
